Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Tom Lindahl <d2l...@dtek.chalmers.se> wrote:
>1. Does a vampire have to be untapped to play reaction cards?...

Yes.

>2. How fast can you sacrifice the edge? If you have the edge and a threat
> counter, you might wan't to hang on to the edge for some reason (like
> if you need it for a vote soon). If you then are succesfully bled can
> you fast as hell sacrifice the edge before your predator gets it.
> (Naturally the predator would get it, but before or after the sacrifice?)

You can turn the edge in whenever you feel like it (I'm assuming you're asking
about Sabbat Threat and such).

>3. When are you allowed to play Cat's guidance? It say's immediately after
> the vampire blocks or something like that, but is this the very second
> the block is succesful or right after the ensuing combat?

You would play it just before the combat begins.

>4. If you have three short term investments in play, can you take 3 blood
> from them (1 each) each master phase? I think you should only be allowed
> to take one since you take one blood instead of playing a master card.

You spend a master action to take one counter off one Investment. You cannot
take off multiple Investment counters without multiple master actions.

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Any combat resulting from blocking an action happens after the action has
been blocked. The state of "blocking an action" doesn't really carry through
the combat, even though people talk about the "blocking minion" when combat
is discussed. Cat's Guidance must be used just before combat begins.

Messages.Author: Joe Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3d0961$r...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>,

Thomas R Wylie <aa...@cats.ucsc.edu> wrote:
>
>Any combat resulting from blocking an action happens after the action has
>been blocked. The state of "blocking an action" doesn't really carry through
>the combat, even though people talk about the "blocking minion" when combat
>is discussed. Cat's Guidance must be used just before combat begins.
>

Then how can Form of Mist work? It's still pretty nebulous. Combat
can be thought of as the actual blocking of the action, after all (Rake
stops Democritus from calling a vote by throwing a car at him). And
Form of Mist will let the action continue, implicitly arguing that the
action isn't done with until combat is over. That's the conceptual
arguement. Next is the logistical arguement (they're two separate
arguements).

If both of these cards come together, you get a paradox under this
ruling that isn't there under the after combat ruling. Say Wynn blocks
Badger. Wynn then plays Cat's Guidance and they go into combat. Badger
strikes with Form of Mist, and the action continues. Now Wynn hasn't
successfully blocked the action, so he couldn't have played Cat's
Guidance. Oops. If the action isn't over until after the combat, then
Wynn doesn't get the chance to play it at all, and there's no paradox
since the action isn't successfully blocked by him.

The only reason that I can think of to have CG be limited to before
combat is to prevent drawing one in the middle of combat. But since
drawing and immediately using cards is one of the features of this
game, that's not really a concern.

>>is discussed. Cat's Guidance must be used just before combat begins.

>Then how can Form of Mist work?...

It breaks the rules.

>ruling that isn't there under the after combat ruling. Say Wynn blocks
>Badger. Wynn then plays Cat's Guidance and they go into combat. Badger
>strikes with Form of Mist, and the action continues. Now Wynn hasn't

>successfully blocked the action...

Wynn *did* block the action. Form of Mist just allows the action to
continue anyway, which normally can't happen.
